_purpose: Independent Netra-track dataset -- deliberately NOT derived from eval/local/dataset.json at runtime (a separate, authored copy), so the two tracks can diverge on purpose without one script silently changing what the other scores. Same underlying source of truth (the live cybersierra manifest) as the local dataset, just a separate curated selection -- see eval/README.md's 'Two independent dataset definitions' section for why.

generated_from.note: The manifest changed between this repo's initial build and this dataset's capture (notifications module and several tprm resources -- activity-logs, assessee-scans, assessee-tenant-users -- were added by a self-update in between). This dataset is a snapshot; see verify/validate_query_dataset.py for drift detection against whatever manifest is live when you run it.

example_queries: Is the Cyber Sierra backend up right now?

single_command_queries.description: List in-app notifications for the caller (filters/paging via --data)
example_queries: Show me my notifications from the last week.
List all my assessment-related notifications since May 2026.
single_command_queries.notes: Manifest description explicitly warns paging defaults to 10 rows and is a nested {page,limit} object under --data -- worth an example where the Executor/Planner needs to set an explicit limit.

single_command_queries.description: Unread notification count for the caller
example_queries: How many unread notifications do I have?
What permission policies apply to the compliance-auditor role?
Show me the access policies for the auditor role subject.
single_command_queries.notes: subject is required and not obviously a userId or a role name from the description alone -- a good case for the Executor's {{inputs.*}} collection step (contracts.md: 'Collects any unresolved {{inputs.*}} values from the user').

single_command_queries.description: Valid filter values for activity logs (actors, object types)
example_queries: What filter options are available for activity logs on assessee 118898?
single_command_queries.notes: objectType is an enum (assessee/document/comment) -- a plausible case for the model to get wrong without reading the manifest params carefully.

composite_queries.example_query: Give me a quick compliance snapshot: how many vendors do we have, and what's on the risk dashboard?
composite_queries.notes: No data dependency between the two steps -- tests that the Planner can produce two independent, parallel-eligible (but still linearly executed, per execution-plan-schema.md's 'strictly linear') steps from one request.

composite_queries.example_query: Who am I, and how many unread notifications do I have?
List our vendors, then show me the full details of the first one.
composite_queries.notes: Step 2's id argument should be a {{step[1].*}} reference into step 1's list output -- the canonical case execution-plan-schema.md's Reference Syntax exists for.

adversarial_queries.reason: No email/report-delivery command exists anywhere in the manifest. Per planning-rules.md's rejection criteria, this should be rejected outright, not approximated with a partial plan.
